Tooling and software products
Products a SaaS team uses to build, run, sell or support its software.
Say what the product does, who it is for and which stage of a company it suits.
Say how a founder gets it and what it costs the founder.
WE does not say that WE uses or recommends a product.

Cloud services and credits
Programs that give early-stage companies cloud usage credits or similar allowances.
Say who qualifies, how a company applies and when the credits expire.
Say what happens when the credits run out.
WE does not promise that a founder will receive credits.

Legal services
Firms that advise early-stage companies on formation, contracts and regulation.
Say which jurisdictions the firm covers and which matters it takes on.
Say how the firm bills a founder.
WE does not give legal advice.
WE does not choose a firm for a founder.
Finance and accounting
Firms that keep the books, taxes and financial reporting of young companies in order.
Say which services the firm provides and which size of company it works with.
WE does not give tax advice.
WE does not handle a founder's money.
Engineering and delivery services
Teams that deliver engineering, design or operations work alongside a founder's own team.
Say which skills the team covers and how it hands work over.
Say how the team is managed and how it bills for its work.
WE steers its own dedicated teams and manages their subcontractors, and an enquiry does not change that.
A delivery partner is a category here, and WE lists none.
Ecosystem and community programs
Communities, events and resource programs that support founders.
Say who the program is for, how a founder joins and what it asks of a member.
Say who runs the program.
WE does not promise a founder a place in any program.
WE names no program on this site.

How the pieces fit
A founder applies.
WE scopes the work with the founder and seats a dedicated team for that company.
The team is made of defined roles, WE steers it, and WE manages any subcontractors it uses.
As the work produces evidence, WE helps the founder organize that evidence so a serious investor can read it.
Each step has its own page.
The founder page says what WE asks of you and what you keep doing.
The operators page lists the roles that can staff a seat.
The investors page says what WE does for companies preparing to raise, and what it does not do.
The partners page says how an organization that helps founders can send WE an enquiry.
Partners
An organization that helps or equips founders may send WE an enquiry.
The partners page lists six categories, from tooling and software products to ecosystem and community programs.
An enquiry creates no partnership, no referral arrangement and no commitment on either side.

The standards WE works to
WE steers a team with a small set of documented operating frameworks.
Those are described on the frameworks page.
The public standards WE maps its work to are named on the trust center.
Naming a standard is a statement about what WE reads and works from.
It is not a claim of certification for WE or for any company.
What the network is not
There is no logo wall, no client list and no investor network.
If that changes, it will appear on its own page with the names of people and companies who agreed in writing to be named.
Investor Introductions is a separate, paid add-on.
It is not a membership of any network.
